A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoRA-FAIR. All 13 pages of v2 and 15 pages of v3, including their supplementary material, support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original federated fine-tuning experiments on DomainNet and NICO++, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, convergence curves, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in the main paper and supplementary material.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the residual correction to B, regularized objective, SGD solution, and client initialization procedure. Section 11's new Frobenius-norm analysis does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DomainNet categories and NICO++ domains for image classification under feature non-IID and combined feature/label non-IID conditions. No dataset, task, or evaluated domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain Centralized, FFA-LoRA, FedIT, FLoRA, and FlexLoRA. Table 6 retains HETLoRA and FlexLoRA, and the remaining comparisons also retain their comparator sets. Newly cited methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The model configurations, client participation, Dirichlet parameter, batch size, local training budgets, and global rounds are unchanged. Appendix heterogeneous-rank settings and the local-epoch versus global-round comparison are also retained.

E4.justification: The initialization comparisons, residual-position ablation, regularization and rank sensitivity studies, convergence curves, computational overhead analysis, and FLoRA reinitialization analysis are unchanged. v2 supplementary Sections 8.1–8.4 become v3 Sections 9.1–9.4.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over three independent runs, retain the same plus/minus reporting in Tables 2–3, and describe the shaded regions in Figures 7–8 as variance across runs. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The empirical values and findings match throughout Tables 2–7 and Figures 2–9. For example, Table 2 retains LoRA-FAIR's ViT average accuracies of 77.07 on DomainNet and 91.24 on NICO++. No empirical result entries are added.

T1.justification: v3 adds Section 11, absent from v2: a squared-Frobenius objective and closed-form correction, an approximation-bound theorem, an exact-recovery corollary, and a convergence theorem with proofs under smoothness and bounded-gradient assumptions. These constitute substantial new formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about jointly addressing aggregation bias and initialization lag while maintaining efficiency and outperforming federated baselines. The added theory does not revise these main contribution statements.

C2.justification: Section 11 newly argues that increasing data heterogeneity enlarges aggregation error and that LoRA-FAIR's contraction factor produces especially tighter convergence bounds in highly non-IID settings. Existing empirical interpretations and applicability discussions are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including the pretrained model identifiers, optimizer settings, and server optimization using SGD with learning rate 0.01 for 1000 iterations. No new code/data access information or hardware details appear.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to FedBCGD, momentum-based stochastic controlled weight averaging, and FedPETuning. Section 6 expands its FL citations and includes FedPETuning alongside FedIT as a federated-LoRA precedent; the broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises the author/affiliation block and equal-contribution note, adds acknowledgments and a theorem section, and makes limited related-work edits. Existing sections and narrative remain largely intact, with supplementary sections renumbered.

P2.justification: The same nine figures and seven tables are retained. The author block is condensed, caption spacing and page flow change, and some tables move within pages, notably Table 4 from the right column to the left column. The plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional references modestly broaden coverage, but the principal addition introduces invalid general guarantees. In Section 11, Equation (16) overlooks the nullspace of the wide matrix A-bar: full row rank does not ensure that an arbitrary target update lies in its row space. This undermines Theorem 11.1's contraction bound, Corollary 11.2's exact recovery, and the factor reused in Theorem 11.3. With the method and empirical evidence unchanged, these unsupported theoretical assurances create a limited net decline in mathematical reliability.
